rules.statement: Don't report reading `IOptions<T>.Value` in a constructor or primary-constructor initializer when the type deliberately builds its state once from startup-fixed options and those options are registered with `ValidateOnStart()`.
rules.why: `IOptions<T>` is reserved for values fixed at startup, so building once from it is intended, and `ValidateOnStart` makes a bad configuration stop the host before the first request.
rules.check: Before reporting, look at the options registration for `AddOptions<T>().ValidateOnStart()` with a validator, and at sibling types that build the same way. Report only if the type uses `IOptionsMonitor`/`IOptionsSnapshot` semantics or nothing validates on start.

rules.statement: When a change removes a package reference from a shipping package, name every package consumers no longer receive transitively in the CHANGELOG entry and tell them to reference it directly.
rules.why: A consumer that used those APIs through the transitive reference stops compiling on upgrade without warning.
rules.check: For a diff that removes a `PackageReference` from a packable project, check that the CHANGELOG entry lists the dropped transitive packages.

rules.statement: Run timeouts, retries and other time-dependent logic on an injected `TimeProvider`, and test them with `FakeTimeProvider` and explicit gates such as `TaskCompletionSource`, not real timers or delays.
rules.why: Tests that rely on real short timers are slow and flaky. A fake clock makes retry and timeout tests deterministic.
rules.check: Look for time-based policies or `Task.Delay` that don't use the registered `TimeProvider`, and for tests that depend on real millisecond timers.

rules.statement: Compare HTTP status codes against named `HttpStatusCode` members, such as `HttpStatusCode.TooManyRequests` and `>= HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError`, not bare numeric literals.
rules.why: Bare literals like 408, 429 and 500 don't say which statuses they mean.
rules.check: Look for status-code comparisons against integer literals.

rules.statement: Declare static methods, along with constants and static fields, at the top of a type, before its instance members.
rules.why: The house member order puts constants and statics at the top of the type, and that includes static methods, not just fields.
rules.check: Look for static methods declared after instance properties or methods in the same type.

rules.statement: Give every public method in a benchmark project, including `[GlobalSetup]` and `[Benchmark]` methods, a `/// <summary>` saying what it sets up or measures, plus `<returns>` when it returns a value.
rules.why: The rule that every added type or member gets a doc comment applies to non-packable benchmark projects too.
rules.check: Look for new public benchmark or setup methods without XML doc comments.
